```{python}
from collections import Counter
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

import re


#PART 1
#IMPORTING
try:
    with open("../../../data/gutenberg/moby.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        moby_lines = f.readlines()
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Couldn't find that file — check the filename and location.")

while not moby_lines[0].startswith("*** START"):
    moby_lines = moby_lines[1:]     
moby_lines = moby_lines[1:]        

while not moby_lines[-1].startswith("*** END"):
    moby_lines = moby_lines[:-1]    
moby_lines = moby_lines[:-1]       

moby_text = "".join(moby_lines)



try:
    with open("../../../data/gutenberg/rnj.txt", "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        rnj_lines = f.readlines()
except FileNotFoundError:
    print("Couldn't find that file — check the filename and location.")

while not rnj_lines[0].startswith("*** START"):
    rnj_lines = rnj_lines[1:]   
rnj_lines = rnj_lines[1:]         

while not rnj_lines[-1].startswith("*** END"):
    rnj_lines = rnj_lines[:-1]    
rnj_lines = rnj_lines[:-1]       

rnj_text = "".join(rnj_lines)

#code grabs the text from each book and saves it as a list callead 'book'_lines
#the lines are then cleaned up a bit by chopping off everything before the start of the actual text and the lines after the end of the text
#the paired down lines are smooshed together into 'book'_text


#CLEANING
import re

moby_words = re.split(r"[\W]+", moby_text.lower())
moby_words = [w for w in moby_words if w != ""]

rnj_words = re.split(r"[\W]+", rnj_text.lower())
rnj_words = [w for w in rnj_words if w != ""]

#the text is cleaned using the split function, breakng things up into individual words and making the whole thing lower case, skipping blanks
#END PART 1  

#PART 2
#TTR
moby_ttr = len(set(moby_words)) / len(moby_words)
rnj_ttr = len(set(rnj_words)) / len(rnj_words)
print("moby types:",len(set(moby_words)))
print("moby tokens:",len(moby_words))
print("rnj types:",len(set(rnj_words)))
print("rnj tokens:",len(rnj_words))
print("moby TTR:", moby_ttr)
print("rnj TTR:", rnj_ttr)

#find the type token ration by dividing the number of unique words by the number of total words in each text
#print that along with the tokens and type counts

moby_ttr_10000 = len(set(moby_words[:10000])) / len(moby_words[:10000])
rnj_ttr_10000 = len(set(rnj_words[:10000])) / len(rnj_words[:10000])
print("moby TTR (10,000 words):", moby_ttr_10000)
print("rnj TTR (10,000 words):", rnj_ttr_10000)

#finds a sample from just 10,000 words to account for different overall size of each text, which affects the ttr due to the build of of function words like "the"

#WORD LENGTH
moby_wd_len_total = 0
for w in moby_words:
    moby_wd_len_total += len(w)
moby_avg_word_len = moby_wd_len_total / len(moby_words)

rnj_wd_len_total = 0
for w in rnj_words:
    rnj_wd_len_total += len(w)
rnj_avg_word_len = rnj_wd_len_total / len(rnj_words)

print("rnj Average Word Length:", rnj_avg_word_len)
print("moby Average Word Length:", moby_avg_word_len)

#makes variable to store total wordlength and fills it up by going through the text and adding value for each words length
#then divides that total length by the total number of words to get the average length of any word
#END PART 2

#PART 3
#LY 
moby_ly =[w for w in moby_words if w .endswith("ly")]
rnj_ly=[w for w in rnj_words if w .endswith("ly")]

moby_ly_rate = len(moby_ly) / len(moby_words) * 1000
rnj_ly_rate = len(rnj_ly) / len(rnj_words) * 1000

print ("moby ly:",moby_ly_rate)
print ("rnj ly:",rnj_ly_rate)
#looks for words within each text that end in 'ly' then creates a ratio per 1000 words to account for difference in overall length.
#UN
moby_un =[w for w in moby_words if w .startswith("un")]
rnj_un=[w for w in rnj_words if w .startswith("un")]

moby_un_rate = len(moby_un) / len(moby_words) * 1000
rnj_un_rate = len(rnj_un) / len(rnj_words) * 1000

print ("moby un:",moby_un_rate)
print ("rnj un:",rnj_un_rate)
#checks for words starting with "un" then does the same ratio
#ING
moby_ing =[w for w in moby_words if w .endswith("ing")]
rnj_ing=[w for w in rnj_words if w .endswith("ing")]

moby_ing_rate = len(moby_ing) / len(moby_words) * 1000
rnj_ing_rate = len(rnj_ing) / len(rnj_words) * 1000

print ("moby ing:",moby_ing_rate)
print ("rnj ing :",rnj_ing_rate)
#same but with 'ing'
#NESS
moby_ness =[w for w in moby_words if w .endswith("ness")]
rnj_ness=[w for w in rnj_words if w .endswith("ness")]

moby_ness_rate = len(moby_ness) / len(moby_words) * 1000
rnj_ness_rate = len(rnj_ness) / len(rnj_words) * 1000

print ("moby ness:",moby_ness_rate)
print ("rnj ness:",rnj_ness_rate)
#same but with 'ness'
#DIALOGUE
moby_quote = [w for w in moby_words if w .startswith("\"")]
rnj_quote =  [w for w in rnj_words if w .startswith("\"")]

moby_quote_rate = len(moby_quote) / len(moby_words) * 1000
rnj_quote_rate = len(rnj_quote) / len(rnj_words) * 1000

print ("moby quote:",moby_quote_rate)
print("rnj quote:",rnj_quote_rate)
#checks for lines staring with '"', using '\' to search properly
#COMMON WORDS
moby_counter = Counter(moby_words)
top10 = moby_counter.most_common(10)

stopwords = ["the", "to", "and", "of", "a", "her", "i", "in", "was", "it",
             "she", "he", "be", "that", "you", "not", "had", "as", "his", "for",
             "with", "is", "have", "but", "at", "so", "all", "my", "been", "him",
             "on", "by", "could", "would", "very", "no", "what", "which", "they",
             "were", "there", "me", "an", "must", "this", "said", "from", "or",
             "will", "any", "much", "than", "such", "their", "them", "if", "do",
             "did", "one", "when", "your", "more", "are", "we", "who", "up",
             "out", "down", "into", "s", "t", "thee", "thy", "thou", "d", "ye", "now", "like", "then", "some", "upon", "shall", "_"]
             #ADDED 'YE' 'THY' 'THEE' 'THOU' AND 'D' TO STOPWORDS TO ACCOUNT FOR SAILOR/SHAKSPEARIAN VOCAB

moby_content_words = [w for w in moby_words if w not in stopwords]

moby_top10 = Counter(moby_content_words).most_common(10)
moby_labels = [pair[0] for pair in moby_top10]
moby_freqs = [pair[1] for pair in moby_top10]

rnj_counter = Counter(rnj_words)
top10 = rnj_counter.most_common(10)

stopwords = ["the", "to", "and", "of", "a", "her", "i", "in", "was", "it",
             "she", "he", "be", "that", "you", "not", "had", "as", "his", "for",
             "with", "is", "have", "but", "at", "so", "all", "my", "been", "him",
             "on", "by", "could", "would", "very", "no", "what", "which", "they",
             "were", "there", "me", "an", "must", "this", "said", "from", "or",
             "will", "any", "much", "than", "such", "their", "them", "if", "do",
             "did", "one", "when", "your", "more", "are", "we", "who", "up",
             "out", "down", "into", "s", "t", "thee", "thy", "thou", "d", "ye", "now", "like", "then", "some", "upon", "shall", "_"]

rnj_content_words = [w for w in rnj_words if w not in stopwords]


rnj_top10 = Counter(rnj_content_words).most_common(10)
rnj_labels = [pair[0] for pair in rnj_top10]

print("top ten words in Moby Dick:",moby_top10)
print("top ten words in Romeo and Juliet:",rnj_top10)
#sets up a counter with the text

plt.bar(["Mody Dick", "Romeo and Juliet"], [moby_ly_rate, rnj_ly_rate])
plt.title("frequency of 'ly' in Moby Dick and Romeo and Juliet")
plt.xlabel("source")
```
